question: How do privacy-tool effect estimates differ between raw API-pattern candidates and evidence-supported browser-profile collection on a purposive website sample?

sample.origin: Purposive consent-verifiable sample assembled from public Cookiebot technology lists, earlier project TCF checks and related-work CMP test sites; provenance and exclusions are frozen in sites_final_experiment.audit.md.
sample.selection: Sites were selected only from access and consent verification performed before the final fingerprinting experiment. Fingerprinting outcomes were not inspected or used for selection. This is not a probability sample or a representative web sample.
sample.eligibility: Report all 53 attempted candidates. Final comparisons require successful paired navigation and, for accept/reject+GPC, a confirmed saved Cookiebot or loaded GDPR-applicable TCF choice after reload. Sites that changed after screening remain documented exclusions rather than being replaced.
sample.no_replacement: Do not replace failures after inspecting protection outcomes. Related domains may share ownership; no independent-owner/population inference.

procedure: Single pass through the 53 candidates in four conditions (212 scheduled site-visits). Seeded randomized condition and site order, shared site order across conditions, fresh profile per site/condition, fixed Netherlands VPN exit, en-US locale, Europe/Amsterdam timezone, 5 second dwell and no subpages. Earlier validation batches are retained separately; the single final pass does not independently establish temporal repeatability.
detector: Frozen evidence-v3 six-family candidate rules. Attribute enumeration requires four distinct successful Navigator/Screen reads per script/document; candidates are not confirmed fingerprinting.

review.reviewer: Codex main reviewer; source-assisted single-reviewer provisional assessments. No independent agreement/accuracy claim without a separate completed review.
review.supported_collection: Observed successful operations plus callsite-linked source establish assembly of multiple browser/device properties into a client/device model used for analytics, advertising, identity or anti-abuse; or source/payload/initiator corroboration establishes transmission of that model. Document properties, source hashes and code locations, purpose basis and evidence strength. Neither domain reputation, a keyword, nor mere co-occurrence is sufficient.
review.ordinary_usage: Every observed operation in the counted pair has a concrete functional explanation supported by code context, with no observed supported collection in that pair. This does not certify the vendor or entire script as benign.
review.uncertain: Use when purpose, executed source version, attribution or combination/use is insufficiently established; do not force a decision. Missing matches are not evidence of absence.
review.pair_aggregation: Any supported observation makes its site/condition/domain/technique pair supported. Ordinary requires all observations ordinary. Any unresolved observation otherwise keeps the pair uncertain. Unreviewed is distinct from uncertain.
not_claimed: tracking intent solely from profile assembly
review.version_control: Freeze before final visits; deviations require a dated amendment and separate sensitivity analysis. Existing inspected sites/patterns are development examples, not held-out accuracy validation.

metrics.unit: Unique (site, condition, repetition, script eTLD+1 domain, technique) pair over after_consent/home_reload; landing diagnostic only.
metrics.primary: Paired per-site raw and reviewed net count reduction: 1 - treatment/baseline. Supported-only reductions are descriptive comparisons of lower bounds until all labels are decisive.
metrics.uncertainty: For fully reviewed pairs: B_min=supported baseline, B_max=B_min+uncertain baseline, T_min=supported treatment, T_max=T_min+uncertain treatment; reduction lies between 1-T_max/B_min and 1-T_min/B_max where denominators exist. Undefined denominators stay undefined. These bounds are not confidence intervals.
metrics.secondary: Baseline-pair survival, disappearance and treatment-only pairs are reported separately from net reductions; same-key persistence is not proof of identical code.
metrics.repetition: Report per-round counts and paired eligibility. Complete-site analyses keep all repetitions of a website together; no treating repetitions as independent sites. Bootstrap intervals are exploratory and undefined resamples are not silently discarded.
metrics.attribution_sensitivity: Retain generated-source/missing-body pairs as uncertain; do not merge them with another script without verified execution/source identity. Report code hashes/callsite diagnostics alongside domain counts.
metrics.interpretation: No systematic underestimation claim unless supported across the selected sample; outcomes may show higher, lower, unchanged or unresolved estimates. Rejection+GPC is a combined intervention, not separate effects.
